about: Synthetic engineering meeting for evaluating summaries (#70). Every name, number, product, and ticket is invented. It plants: a ticket number, a quoted error and an HTTP status, a self-corrected value, a product misspelled in the transcript but spelled in the notes, a configuration change and what it proved, a how-to explanation, and tasks with owners and a conditional plan. Each expect entry lists accepted spellings separated by |.
title: Billing sync
notes:
- SUP-4821 duplicate charges
- Corvina retry setting?
- how to export a test user
segments: Okay, let's get started. The main thing today is SUP-4821, the duplicate charges ticket.
Right. So Dana here. We confirmed it yesterday afternoon. Customers on the Lakeside tenant got charged twice for the October renewal.
How many customers are we talking about?
Forty-two accounts so far. Every one of them is on Lakeside, none on the other tenants.
And do we know why it's only Lakeside?
That's the interesting part. Lakeside is the only tenant that still has auto retry turned on in Corvena.
When the payment call times out, Corvena retries it, but the first charge actually went through. So the customer gets charged twice.
So the timeout is the real trigger. What's timing out?
The payment gateway. In the logs we see it return a 503, sorry, not a 503, it's a 502, bad gateway, about four seconds into the call.
And then on the retry we get this error in our service: token exchange failed: invalid_grant.
Is the invalid_grant a separate bug, or part of the same thing?
Marcus thinks it's the same thing. The retry reuses the token from the first attempt, and that token was already spent.
Marcus here. Yeah, the token is single use, so the second attempt can never succeed on its own. It only looks like a failure.
Okay. So what did we try?
This morning I turned off auto retry for Lakeside in the Corvena admin console, at about nine thirty.
Since then we've had zero duplicate charges, and we've had eleven gateway timeouts in that window. So turning off retry stopped the duplicates.
That's pretty convincing. Any downside to leaving retry off?
The downside is that a real failure won't get retried automatically, so a customer whose payment genuinely failed has to retry it themselves.
Support would see more of those tickets. It's probably a handful a week.
I can live with that for now. The bigger worry is whether other tenants could hit this if someone turns retry back on.
Agreed. There's no alert for this either. We only found it because a customer emailed us with two receipts.
Let's talk about refunds. Who's handling the forty-two accounts?
Dana again. I can issue the refunds from the billing dashboard, it's about two hours of work. I'll start today.
Great. And we should email those customers before they notice.
I'll draft the email, and Marcus can review it.
Next thing, I keep forgetting how to export a test user so we can reproduce this. Can someone walk me through it?
Sure. Open the Corvena admin console, go to Accounts, and search for the test account by email.
Then open the account, click the three dots in the top right, and choose Export as JSON.
Save that file, and when you want to log in as that user later, you use Import from JSON on the same page.
Got it, Accounts, three dots, Export as JSON, then Import later. Thanks.
Okay, what about the gateway itself? Are we talking to the vendor?
Marcus. I opened a case with them yesterday. Their status page says everything's fine, which doesn't match what we see.
If they don't respond by Friday, I think we should roll back the 4.2 release, because the timeouts started the day 4.2 shipped.
That's a good catch. Is that a coincidence, or did 4.2 change something about the gateway calls?
4.2 lowered our client timeout from ten seconds to five. So calls that used to finish in six or seven seconds now count as timeouts.
So we might be causing the timeouts ourselves.
Possibly. Raising the timeout back to ten seconds would be the quick test.
Let's do that before we roll anything back. Marcus, can you raise it on staging today and watch it overnight?
Okay. So to recap the plan. Dana does refunds and the customer email.
Marcus raises the client timeout to ten seconds on staging today, and keeps the vendor case going.
If the vendor hasn't answered by Friday and staging still shows timeouts, we roll back 4.2.
And I'll write up an alert for duplicate charges so we hear about this before a customer does.
